evidence.quote: A: Accessory renal arteries in patients with complex abdominal aortic aneurysms (CAAAs) and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

B: Extension of the bridging stent-graft into both the anterior and posterior divisions of the internal iliac artery with an iliac branch device, specifically for internal iliac artery aneurysms with unsuitable sealing zones.
C: Incorporation of a replaced or aberrant hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery in cases of complex aortic disease.

D: Aortic arch aneurysms requiring repair into Zone 0, incorporating the use of bridging stent-grafts in the right common carotid artery and right subclavian artery when the brachiocephalic trunk is unsuitable as a landing zone.

A: After successful cannulation of the lower renal artery, the first balloon-expandable stent-graft with a doubled PTFE layer and sandwiched open-cell stent structure is deployed, establishing a stable connection to the directional branch. The directional branch is intentionally positioned higher than usual to allow for optimal graft alignment and future deployment of the secondary stent-grafts into the accessory renal artery.
B: The in-stent in situ fenestration is created 2 cm distal to the edge of the directional branch using the Outback Elite reentry catheter (Cordis, Santa Clara, California).
C: After the exchange of the reentry catheter for a 3 mm angioplasty balloon, the in situ fenestration is predilated to prepare for catheterization of the accessory renal artery.
D: Following the successful selective catheterization of the second target vessel, the second balloon-expandable bridging stent is deployed.

E: Finally, the “buddy” system is used, with a 0.018 inch angioplasty balloon positioned in the BIS2T overlapping area through the accessory renal artery. A third balloon-expandable stent is deployed into the main renal artery in a kissing balloon technique to achieve a double “D-shaped” conformation. The final configuration is confirmed by noncontrast CBCT and angiography prior to the removal of the guidewires, ensuring the desired graft shape and function.

Phantom model setup for technical evaluation of the BIS2T procedure. The setup consists of a perforated plastic plate, serving as the anchoring structure. Attached to it are plastic hoses of varying diameters: a 30 mm diameter plastic hose cranially, representing the distal thoracic aorta into which the main body of the branched stent-graft device is deployed. An 18 mm hose distally secures the stent-graft in place, while two 6 mm plastic hoses are closely positioned and fixed laterally to simulate the target vessels. This phantom model is used for the technical assessment of the procedure, ensuring proper deployment and stability of the stent-graft system in different vessel sizes.

claims.text: A 70-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, morbid obesity and cigarette-smoking history developed increasing mid-abdominal pain for several days with a large tender/pulsatile abdominal mass. CTA showed a symptomatic 6.1 cm Extent IV thoracoabdominal aneurysm involving celiac, SMA, right renal and two left renal arteries (4.5/4 mm). Chronic right common iliac occlusion had collateral reconstitution without claudication. Under general anesthesia, left femoral/axillary access and systemic heparinization, multibranch endovascular repair incorporated mesenteric/right renal targets and preserved both left renal arteries using BIS2T. Completion angiography showed patent stents and adequate renal flow without endoleak, dissection or embolization. Recovery had no reported complications; six-month clinical/imaging follow-up showed patency without endoleak, sac expansion or integrity issues. Generic phantom results and recommended techniques are not additional patient findings.

Bilateral anterior/posterior division branches were patent, measuring 4/8 mm. Endovascular repair was recommended with E-tegra/bilateral E-iliac devices. The documented procedure used general anesthesia and bilateral femoral access; left BIS2T repair and completion angiography preceded identical right repair and final aortic graft/limb placement. Final right IIA angiography documented successful incorporation of both divisions. Postoperative/follow-up CTA showed patent grafts without the documented vascular complications. Neither patient was reported to have complications; Case 2 follow-up duration was not stated and is not borrowed from Case 1.

The patient’s medical history was notable for hypertension, cigarette smoking, and ischemic cardiomyopathy with no active symptoms. A CTA revealed a 3.7 cm infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, bilateral 3 cm common iliac artery aneurysms, 4.9 cm right and 4.1 cm left IIAAs. Endovascular repair was recommended using E-tegra (Artivion, CryoLife Jotec, Atlanta, Georgia) bifurcated stent-graft and bilateral E-iliac Iliac Branch devices (Artivion CryoLife Jotec) with preservation of bilateral anterior and posterior divisional branches using BIS2T.

evidence.quote: The patient was treated under general endotracheal anesthesia in a hybrid operating room with fixed GE Discovery system. Bilateral percutaneous femoral access was established in standard fashion using preclosure technique. Through-and-through femoral-femoral access was established. The left E-iliac was loaded in the aortic guidewire and the femoral-femoral guidewire, advanced into the proximal left common iliac artery and deployed with the directional branch 1 cm proximal to the origin of the aneurysmal left IIA. A 12 Fr flexible Dryseal sheath (WL Gore) was advanced up and over the aortic bifurcation and into the portal, followed by selective catheterization of the left IIAA. The first balloon-expandable VBX stent-graft (8Large×79 mm) was deployed from the directional branch to the aneurysm sac. The proximal portion of the stent-graft was postdilated with a 10 mm angioplasty balloon to stabilize the stent-graft at the directional branch. An in situ fenestration was created in the VBX stent-graft using Outback Elite reentry catheter and a 0.014 inch PT2 guidewire (Boston Scientific) was advanced into the aneurysm sac, followed by removal of the reentry catheter and predilatation of the fenestration with a 3 mm angioplasty balloon. A 4 Fr vertebral catheter was advanced via the in situ fenestration and used for selective catheterization of the anterior divisional branch. The second balloon-expandable VBX stent-graft was advanced via a Rosen guidewire (Cook Medical Inc) and deployed via the in situ fenestration into the anterior divisional branch with approximately 1 cm overlap into the first VBX stent-graft. The posterior divisional branch was selectively catheterized via the first VBX stent-graft and a third VBX stent-graft was deployed into the posterior divisional branch overlapping into the first VBX stent-graft. Kissing balloon angioplasty of the overlapping area of the BIS2T was performed using 5 and 6 mm angioplasty balloons. Selective left IIA branch completion angiography was performed which showed a widely patent bifurcated stent-graft system with no dissection, endoleak or embolization. The right contralateral IIAA was treated in identical fashion, followed by placement of the bifurcated aortic stent-graft and connecting iliac limb extensions. Follow-up CTA revealed no evidence of endoleak and widely patent stent-grafts (Figure 7).
